modelScope.variant: Full-size EN Vigilon 4/6-loop panel with 2 km loop cards
modelScope.menuMapFirmware: EN54 (V4), MCC/MCB V4.53 or higher as printed in Appendix A-1
modelScope.editionBoundary: This is the July 2015 classic full-size family, not a claimed match for Vigilon Plus, Compact, Compact VA, Nano or every later firmware revision.
modelScope.practiceConfiguration: Fictional single local panel, two commissioned loops, three zones, six devices; integral printer fitted and initially off.
modelScope.selectionReason: The operator manual and matching dated generic menu appendix provide strong, inspectable source coverage; no market-share claim is made.

sources.title: Vigilon panel and Network node - Operating instructions
sources.edition: July 2015; printed footer issue 4_07-15; metadata and preface describe issue 2
sources.hostType: Manufacturer document mirrored by a fire-system installer
sources.note: Primary operator procedure source. Several internal inconsistencies are explicitly recorded in the audit.

sources.title: Generic Commissioning Instructions for Vigilon 4/6 loop & Compact range of fire panels & network nodes
sources.originalUrlStatus: Returned 404 when independently opened during this audit
sources.hostType: Original Gent manual downloaded from an archive mirror
sources.note: Appendix A-1 covers EN54 (V4) Vigilon with MCC/MCB V4.53 or higher. Compact VA-only and fitted-option branches are excluded or marked conditional. The working archive URL is used for page links.

sources.title: Vigilon VIG1-24 and VIG1-72 installation instructions
sources.note: Printed p12 and pp15-16 confirm up to four/six loop circuits, up to 200 devices per loop and 32-character device / 28-character MCP labels; p48 identifies the issue.

method: Original manufacturer PDF text extraction plus rendered inspection of physical-control pages and Appendix A-1 pages 98-106. Operator instructions take precedence for verified key drills; conflicting or conditional branches remain explicit reference entries.

findings.finding: PDF metadata title and preface say issue 2 / second issue, while the final printed footer says issue 4_07-15.
findings.resolution: Identify the source by document number, July 2015, panel scope and SHA256; preserve both issue descriptions.

findings.finding: Full-size operator instructions repeatedly use loop 1-2 despite p22 describing cards 1-4 and up to six for VIG1-72. Generic appendix selectors allow 1-8.
findings.resolution: The fictional commissioned site has only loops 1 and 2. No claim that two or eight is the hardware capacity of the selected 4/6-loop panel.

findings.finding: Operator device range is 1-200; generic appendix parameter boxes use 1-207.
findings.resolution: Operator forms use the documented 1-200 range and validate against the fictional installed devices. Extended/reserved addresses are not assumed.

findings.finding: Repair p38 says F1 Test/Eng, contradicting the visible F4 top-level mapping, and says F1 Loop after UserCode where PIN-change p21 specifies F1 NewPass.
findings.resolution: Repair is reference-only, with no fabricated exact button lesson.

findings.finding: The narrative orders Test > Zone > On/Off, but the appendix diagram orders Test > Off/On > Zone. It is an engineer-only function.
findings.resolution: Show source explanation and a preconfigured fictional Zone Test scenario; do not offer an exact source-verified F-key route.

findings.finding: Operator p26 says choose FARE with F4 after cycling <etc>; the generic control map positions FARE before <etc>.
findings.resolution: FARE output On/Off is a source-reference branch.

findings.finding: Operator p28 says Aux Rly is F2 after three <etc> presses. p27 says FPE is F2; the appendix page places FARE,FPE,AuxRly in that order.
findings.resolution: Show appendix order in the reference map; Aux Rly operation remains reference-only.

findings.finding: July 2015 operator text describes individual MCP sensing disablement but does not explicitly state MCP behaviour when a zone is disabled. An older 1999 manual differs in scope and is not silently imported.
findings.resolution: The zone-disable lesson uses Zone 2, with no MCP. Full MCP-in-zone behaviour requires panel-specific confirmation.

findings.finding: The p9 indicator table calls the delay-block row Sounder; the physical-face illustration labels it Delay.
findings.resolution: Use the physical-face Delay label and explain its delay-block meaning.

findings.finding: The face artwork repeats 30 in the 17-32 zone row.
findings.resolution: Render the normal continuous zone numbers 1-32 and disclose the artwork discrepancy here.

findings.finding: Within the FPE procedure one line says FARE while its headings, choice and confirmation all say FPE.
findings.resolution: Keep FPE terminology based on the explicit heading, selector and confirmation; FPE operation is reference-only.

findings.finding: View IO label uses F2 Device; Edit IO label explicitly uses F3 Device.
findings.resolution: Preserve each printed route rather than standardising the two.

findings.finding: Display/Print selection is skipped if the printer is absent or switched off.
findings.resolution: Start with a fitted printer switched off and dynamically include output selection when switched on.

findings.finding: AL1, AL2a, AL2b and AL3 have different visibility. Compact VA, D1 voice, SD card, radio, network and Freeblock conditions introduce further branches.
findings.resolution: Customer routes are interactive; engineering and fitted-option branches are clearly marked in the searchable source map.

findings.finding: The keyboard includes Insert, Delete, Shift and cursor keys; the operator text does not fully specify cursor editing semantics.
findings.resolution: FINDR uses a documented training text editor and enforces source label limits; no claim of byte-for-byte firmware editing behaviour.

findings.finding: Display test and Zone Test have approximate documented durations; real alarm behaviour depends on commissioning.
findings.resolution: Use training timing and distinguish rising hint tones from physical panel sounds.

findings.finding: The source documents the clock-field order and controls but does not specify a permitted year range.
findings.resolution: The practice date editor uses 2000-2099 as an explicit FINDR calendar limit, not a claimed Gent hardware or firmware limit.

findings.finding: Params, Cancel and Quit exist in the documentation, but their exact function-key positions are not established independently for every form.
findings.resolution: Live forms show only individually verified route keys. Field guidance is presented as FINDR help; Menu On/Off remains the verified abort control. Active-event result F4 Quit is separately verified by operator p23.

openEvidenceRequests: A recording of the identified full-size panel at customer access showing initial Test/Eng choices after UserCode.
A recording or corrected manufacturer instruction confirming FARE manual-switch and Aux Rly enable/disable function-key positions.
A panel/software-specific confirmation of Zone Test selector order and MCP behaviour under zone disablement.
A firmware/card-specific definition of extended device addresses 201-207 and loop selector values beyond fitted physical loops.
notClaimed: Credential recovery or engineering password generation
